Priya (docs): Heads-up: dashboards/show-cost example in console-observability is aggregating by raw epoch seconds, which means users in non-UTC timezones see shifted daily p95/cost buckets. I spotted it in the EU staging demo.

Jon (eng-runtime): Oof, that's subtle. Is the problem the example query or the dashboard widget timezone fallback?

Priya (docs): Example query uses `floor(ts / 3600) * 3600` for hourly buckets. For CET that becomes misaligned when viewers are in UTC- or +zones. The quick fix is to normalize to UTC in the snippet or use a timezone-aware floor helper.

Nadia (eng-ml): Can you paste the original and suggested snippet? I want to check how it affects the latency SLO graphs we ship in evals.

Priya (docs): Original (simplified):
```sql
SELECT floor(ts/3600)*3600 AS hour, approx_percentile(latency, 0.95) as p95
FROM traces
WHERE service='infer'
GROUP BY hour
ORDER BY hour
```
Suggested (normalize to UTC):
```sql
SELECT date_trunc('hour', to_timestamp(ts) AT TIME ZONE 'UTC') AS hour_utc,
       approx_percentile(latency, 0.95) as p95
FROM traces
WHERE service='infer'
GROUP BY hour_utc
ORDER BY hour_utc
```
This makes the behavior consistent regardless of viewer timezone.

Luis (data-plat): For our backend, ts is stored as integer epoch in seconds. Converting to timestamp + AT TIME ZONE in examples is fine. But we should also add an SDK snippet showing how to generate UTC-normalized buckets client-side for the SDK dashboards (python/js).

Priya (docs): Agreed. Added a short python snippet in the PR showing normalization before uploading sample metrics: `dt = datetime.fromtimestamp(ts, timezone.utc)\nhour = dt.replace(minute=0, second=0, microsecond=0)`

Jon (eng-runtime): Can we keep both options in docs: SQL server-side fix + SDK client-side fix. Add a note under "Common pitfalls" about timezone config on per-user dashboards.

Priya (docs): Done in branch. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/4891 — includes updated quickstart, SQL examples, python/js SDK snippets, and a tiny migration note for customers who import third-party dashboards.

ci-bot: docs-ci / linkcheck warning: docs/console-obsv/quickstart.md references a non-canonical timezone helper link.

Priya (docs): Thanks ci-bot — fixed the link to our time helpers page and updated anchors.

Nadia (eng-ml): Quick question: will this change affect the cached rollups we generate for retention-based cost summaries? If we change the label key name we might break the rollup pipeline.

Luis (data-plat): No pipeline change needed. We're only changing example queries and UI notes. If customers re-ingest with a different bucket key that is their choice. I'll add a note in migration doc clarifying we do not alter stored rollup buckets on import.

Jon (eng-runtime): LGTM. Left two tiny comments in the PR about wording and a test suggestion (add one assertion that the example returns monotonic increasing hours).

Priya (docs): Addressed Jon's comments and added a unit snippet to the quickstart repo tests.

ci-bot: All checks passed — docs-ci green.

Priya (docs): Merged. I'll post a short blurb in #customer-success to flag the migration note and ask support to watch for timezone-related tickets for the next week.

Luis (data-plat): Thanks! I'll run a quick staging smoke to verify dashboard previews render expected UTC buckets.

Nadia (eng-ml): Thanks all. This will help avoid confusion in our latency comparisons across regions.

Priya (docs): Closing thread. If you spot any more timezone oddities in other dashboard examples, please @me. :wave:
